text:
B: Hiya! Oh, you're the engineer! With the binders! I'm Lauren.
A: Craig. Hi. Ja, guilty of the binders.
B: I said in my notes you looked dead organised. Sorry, is that weird? I thought they'd all be labelled.
A: They are labelled. By project number.
B: I knew it! I'm the opposite, me. My kitchen whiteboard's got a shopping list from about March on it. Anyway, how are you? Where are you?
A: Fine, thanks. Woodley, near Reading. I'm originally from Durban, South Africa.
B: Oh wow. I'm Derby. Chaddesden. Thought this was going to be the last one, Danuta told me she'd done four, but here we are, round five.
A: I thought the same. I'd already started thinking about dinner.
B: Chicken and rice, is it? Bethany told me. She said you'd told everyone.
A: Word gets around.
B: It does on here! So what do you do outside work? Bet you're one of them up at six on a Saturday.
A: Er, more or less. I cycle on weekend mornings. On my own. Out towards Henley and back.
B: On your own? I couldn't, I need people. I do parkrun at Markeaton Park, when I can drag myself out of bed. It was freezing Saturday, my hands went purple. But I only go for the chat at the end, honestly, and a coffee.
A: I'd go for the coffee. Not sure about the five K.
B: You cycle to Henley, you'd smash it! I used to teach fitness, at the leisure centre, Zumba, circuits, all that. Till they cut the classes. So I'm looking for work now, and doing the odd cover class.
A: Sorry to hear that. Is there much going?
B: Bits. I applied for ten jobs one night last week and then I've not done one since. That's sort of my problem, I'm all or nothing, do you know what I mean.
A: Ja. Ten in one night is still ten.
B: Oh, that's a nice way of looking at it, actually. Thank you. I'll tell me mum that when she asks.
A: Is she local?
B: Ten minutes away. She rings me three times a day. And me dad's not been well, so she rings even more now. They're doing tests on him.
A: That's hard. Hope it's nothing serious.
B: Me too. You worry, don't you? Are your mum and dad in South Africa still?
A: They are. In Durban. They're in their late seventies. I go back every eighteen months or so. You do worry. There's not much you can do from here except phone.
B: Yeah. At least I can pop round. Sorry, I'm getting all deep, I've been doing that all day on these. So tell me something fun. What music are you into?
A: Same as when I was twenty. Bon Jovi. Dire Straits. Bit of Johnny Clegg.
B: Bon Jovi! Oh, Livin' on a Prayer, I've done a whole step routine to that. The older ladies went mad for it.
A: Glad it's being put to good use.
B: You'd have loved it, everyone stepping off the beat. I'd do the key change and they'd all just stop and scream.
A: That sounds about right for a key change.
B: Ha! Right, I'm doing a Bon Jovi class when I've got my own business going, and you have to—
